topic: The birth and early life of Jesus; John the Baptist

kept.q: Who was sent by God to announce to Mary that she would give birth to Jesus?
kept.explanation: The Bible says the angel Gabriel was sent by God to Mary in Nazareth to tell her she would conceive and bear a son called Jesus. This is recorded in Luke 1:26-31.

kept.q: According to the Gospel of Luke, in which town was Jesus born?
kept.explanation: Luke 2:4-7 records that Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the city of David, when Joseph and Mary travelled there for the census. This fulfilled an Old Testament prophecy about the Messiah's birthplace.

kept.q: Why did Joseph take Mary to Bethlehem shortly before Jesus was born?
options: To register for a census ordered by Caesar Augustus
To pay temple tax to the priests
kept.explanation: Luke 2:1-5 explains that Caesar Augustus ordered a census of the whole Roman world, so Joseph had to go to Bethlehem, his ancestral town, to be registered with Mary.

kept.q: What did John the Baptist eat while he lived in the wilderness?
kept.explanation: Matthew 3:4 describes John the Baptist's diet in the wilderness as locusts and wild honey, showing his simple, disciplined lifestyle as a prophet.

kept.q: What three gifts did the wise men present to the infant Jesus in Bethlehem?
kept.explanation: Matthew 2:11 records that the wise men from the East worshipped the child Jesus and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh, symbols fitting a king, priest, and one who would suffer.

kept.q: Why was Zechariah unable to speak after the angel Gabriel visited him in the temple?
options: He was struck ill by a sudden fever
He had taken a vow of silence
He doubted the angel's message about John's birth
He was overcome with joy and could not talk
kept.explanation: Luke 1:18-20 shows that Zechariah questioned Gabriel's message because he and Elizabeth were old, so the angel made him mute until John was born as a sign and a consequence of his unbelief.

kept.q: Herod the king ordered the killing of baby boys aged two years and under in Bethlehem. Based on the biblical account, what was Herod's main motive for this action?
options: He feared that a rival king had been born who would threaten his throne
He wanted to reduce the population for easier taxation
He was carrying out an order from the Roman governor
He wanted to punish the shepherds for spreading false news
kept.explanation: Matthew 2:3-16 shows Herod was troubled when the wise men asked about the newborn 'king of the Jews', so out of fear for his throne he ordered the massacre of young boys in Bethlehem to eliminate the perceived rival.

kept.q: When Simeon blessed the infant Jesus in the temple, he told Mary that 'a sword will pierce through your own soul also.' Based on the context of Luke's Gospel, what did Simeon mean by this statement?
options: Mary would suffer great sorrow because of what would happen to her son
Mary would be persecuted by Herod's soldiers
Mary would lose her life while fleeing to Egypt
Mary would be rejected by her own family
kept.explanation: Luke 2:34-35 links Simeon's words to the rejection and suffering Jesus would face, which would cause Mary deep personal grief, especially seen later at the crucifixion. It is a prophecy of a mother's sorrow, not physical harm to her.
